title: Agent architectural review and ground-up rebuild

completion_criteria.text: Current-state audit complete: every gap in the roster, the agent definitions and the observation machinery identified with measured evidence from the ledger and the definition files.
Audit delivered in a form the user can read and navigate - a self-contained HTML explainer with diagrams, written for a reader with no prior domain knowledge.
Target architecture designed and approved by the user: roster shape, tool grants, who may delegate, and how the configuration observes itself.
Agent and observer teardown and rebuild executed without breaking the live coupling surface: rules and skills naming agents by string, 405 worktree copies, four backup profiles, derived residuals.
New configuration verified in real use: dispatch routes to the intended agents, and the observation system attributes every run and records an outcome.

spine.active_goal: Rebuild the agent configuration from the ground up - the 13-agent roster and the observer that watches it - with the target architecture approved before any file is touched.
spine.next_step: WAIT for the user's specific instructions on the report and next steps. Do NOT edit any agent, rule, hook or skill file. Round-2 report is delivered at ~/.agent/diagrams/agent-roster-rebuild-recommendations.html: 13 agents in four bands, closed-question termination, and an append-only observer. Six scope questions are settled in 0471. Three items stay open in report section 14: which duplicate skill wins, what fills the three skill gaps, and the unmeasured per-dispatch context cost.
spine.last_session: Designed the 13-agent roster and the observer, delivered in one updated HTML explainer. Rewrote loop termination after the user's critique that it guarded the effect. Probed the binary to settle the frontmatter schema, and ran a live test proving agents do receive rules - on an advisory channel.

open_risks.text: Never read `emitter` in the events log as a measurement — it is a hardcoded constant on every row, and treating it as signal already produced one wrong conclusion
Declare StructuredOutput in tools: on all 13 agents — the new engine fails a census gate if any dispatchable agent omits it, and all 15 current agents omit it today

Settle the claude-security overlap before wiring security-reviewer — that plugin skill is a complete competing pipeline with five sub-agents, so running both yields two unreconciled verdicts on one diff
Decide whether this thread supersedes the paused thread agent-roster-gap-resolution — it covers overlapping ground against an older SPEC and was not touched here
Archive the events log before any teardown step — 8.7 MB across 46 days is the only artifact here that cannot be regenerated, and it is the baseline a new roster gets measured against
Repoint the five skills that name deleted agents — verification-discipline and report break outright, since every branch of their logic invokes verification-strategist and report-writer by name
Land the new mitosis engine before starting the rebuild — this work targets that engine, whose dispatch table comes from engine source literals rather than a static allowlist

key_decisions.title: The audit pass characterises the current state and recommends nothing
Replace all 56 agents with 13 in four bands, with the dispatch tool held only by the Opus leads
Terminate review loops by closing the reviewer's question, not by capping rounds or turns
Rebuild the observer to append one line per run and do everything else at audit time
Put load-bearing rules in agent bodies, generated from shared fragments with a drift check
User rulings on the six open rebuild questions, and the addition of the observer to this thread

out_of_scope: Mutating any agent, rule, hook or skill file until the target architecture at c3 is approved.
